instruction: Wash the rice in 2-3 changes of water until it runs clear.
Boil plenty of water, add rice, cook uncovered 18-20 min until grains are soft.
Drain the starchy water (mar) completely in a strainer.
Rest covered for 5 minutes before serving.
Rinse the brown rice and soak 20 minutes to shorten cooking.
Boil in ample water for 28-32 minutes until tender but chewy.
Drain and rest covered 5 minutes.
Dry-roast the lentil lightly, then wash with the rice.
Temper bay leaf and onion in the oil until golden.
Add turmeric, ginger, potato and stir for a minute.
Add rice, lentil, water and salt; simmer 25 min until soft and porridge-like.
Finish with slit green chillies.
Dry-roast mung dal until fragrant, then wash with the rice and drain.
Fry whole spices and onion in oil until deep golden.
Add ginger-garlic and powdered spices; cook until oil separates.
Add rice and dal, toss 3 minutes, pour in hot water and salt.
Cover and cook on low 20 min; fold in ghee and green chillies, rest 10 min.
Marinate chicken with yoghurt, ginger-garlic, pepper and salt for 30 minutes.
Fry onions in ghee and oil until golden; reserve half as beresta.
Cook the chicken with whole spices until the water dries and oil separates.
Add washed rice, toss, then add hot water, milk powder, sugar and salt.
Cover on very low heat 20 min; rest 10 min, garnish with beresta and chillies.
Marinate beef with yoghurt, ginger-garlic, spices and salt for 1 hour.
Brown the onions in mustard oil and set some aside.
Cook the marinated beef covered until tender and the masala is thick.
Add drained rice, toss well, add hot water and salt.
Cook covered on low 20 min, add green chillies, rest 10 min before serving.
Marinate the goat meat with yoghurt, fried onion, ginger-garlic and all spices for 4 hours.
Par-boil the rice to 70 percent in salted water and drain.
Layer marinated meat and lightly fried potatoes at the bottom of a heavy pot.
Spread the rice over it, drizzle ghee, milk powder and almonds.
Seal the lid with dough and dum-cook on very low heat for 60-75 minutes.
Marinate hilsa steaks with turmeric, mustard paste, yoghurt and salt for 20 minutes.
Fry onions in mustard oil until golden, add ginger-garlic.
Add the fish and cook gently 8 minutes; lift the pieces out carefully.
Add rice to the masala, toss, pour hot water and salt, cook covered 18 min.
Layer the fish and green chillies back on top, add ghee and dum 10 min.
Cook and cool the rice ahead so the grains stay separate.
Stir-fry garlic in hot oil for 30 seconds.
Add carrot, cabbage, peas and capsicum; toss on high heat 3-4 minutes.
Fold in the rice, salt and pepper; toss 3 minutes.
Finish with spring onion.
Cover the previous night's cooked rice with clean water and leave 8-10 hours.
In the morning, loosen the grains by hand.
Serve with salt, raw onion and green chilli.
Rinse the flattened rice quickly and drain in a colander for 10 minutes.
Fry peanuts in oil and set aside; fry potato until cooked.
Add onion, chilli and turmeric, then fold in the drained chira and salt.
Toss 3 minutes on low heat, finish with peanuts, coriander and lemon.
Mix flour and salt, add warm water gradually to a soft dough.
Knead 8 minutes and rest covered 20 minutes.
Divide into 8 balls and roll thin.
Cook on a hot dry tawa 45 seconds each side until it puffs.
Make a soft dough with flour, salt and water; rest 30 minutes.
Roll out each ball, brush with oil, dust with flour and coil into a spiral.
Flatten and roll again to a round.
Shallow-fry on a tawa with a little oil until golden with visible layers.
Rub ghee into the flour with salt, then make a stiff dough with water.
Rest 30 minutes and divide into 12 balls.
Roll into small discs without dusting too heavily.
Slide into hot oil and press gently until they puff; drain on paper.
Mix flour, baking powder, sugar and salt; add yoghurt and milk to a soft dough.
Rest covered in a warm place 1-2 hours.
Shape into ovals, press nigella seeds on top.
Cook on a very hot tawa, flipping once, then brush with ghee.
Grind the sunned rice to a fine flour and sieve it.
Sprinkle salted water in and rub until the flour just holds shape.
Fill small bowls with flour, jaggery and coconut, then top with more flour.
Invert onto a cloth over a steamer and steam 5-7 minutes each.
Soak the rice 4 hours, grind with water to a pourable batter and salt it.
Rest the batter 1 hour.
Heat a small clay or iron mould and pour in a ladle of batter.
Cover and cook 3-4 minutes until set with a lacy top; lift out.
Cook coconut with jaggery until thick and sticky; cool this filling.
Whisk rice flour, maida, semolina, milk, water and salt into a thin batter; rest 30 min.
Pour a thin layer on a lightly oiled pan and cook until the edges lift.
Place filling along one edge and roll up; serve warm.
Cook coconut, jaggery and cardamom to a thick filling and cool.
Boil salted water, stir in the rice flour and knead to a hot dough.
Shape small cups, fill and seal the edges into a crescent.
Steam 12-15 minutes.
Bring salted water to a boil and stir in the rice flour off the heat.
Knead the hot dough until smooth, keeping it covered.
Pat or roll into thin rounds.
Cook on a hot tawa about a minute each side until white and puffed.
Boil washed lentils with turmeric and salt until fully broken down.
Whisk smooth and thin with hot water.
Temper garlic, onion and dried chilli in mustard oil until golden.
Pour the tempering over the dal, add green chilli and coriander.
Boil the lentil with turmeric until soft, keeping it thick.
Fry onion, garlic and ginger in mustard oil until brown.
Add cumin, dried chilli and tomato; cook until the oil separates.
Fold the dal in and simmer 8 minutes until glossy and thick.
Dry-roast the dal until it smells nutty, then wash and boil until just tender.
Temper bay leaf, cumin, onion, garlic and ginger in oil.
Add turmeric and the drained dal, season and stir.
Cook uncovered until dry, finishing with green chillies.
Boil the soaked dal with turmeric and salt until soft but whole.
Fry coconut slivers in ghee until golden and set aside.
Temper whole spices and cumin, add ginger.
Add the dal, sugar and green chilli; simmer 10 minutes and top with coconut.
Boil the washed dal with turmeric and salt until creamy.
Mash lightly with a wooden whisk.
Temper nigella, dried chilli, garlic and onion in mustard oil.
Stir the tempering through and simmer 5 minutes.
Wash the dal well and boil with turmeric and salt until soft.
Whisk to the consistency you like.
Temper garlic, onion and dried chilli in mustard oil.
Combine and simmer briefly with green chillies.
Boil the lentil with turmeric until half done.
Add the diced bottle gourd and salt; cook until translucent.
Temper nigella, garlic and onion in mustard oil.
Stir the tempering and green chillies through and simmer 5 minutes.
Roast, wash and boil the mung dal with turmeric until tender.
Add chopped spinach and cook 5 minutes only.
Temper cumin, garlic and onion in mustard oil.
Combine, season and simmer 5 minutes with green chillies.
Boil the soaked peas with turmeric and salt until they collapse.
Mash roughly with a whisk.
Temper cumin, dried chilli, garlic, ginger and onion in oil.
Stir together and simmer until thick.
Boil the dal with turmeric, tomato and salt until soft.
Whisk to a smooth consistency.
Temper cumin, dried chilli, garlic and onion in oil.
Combine and finish with coriander leaf.
Boil the soaked chickpeas with salt until tender but not mushy.
Fry onion, garlic and ginger in oil until brown.
Add powdered spices with a splash of water and cook until oil separates.
Add chickpeas and potato, simmer until thick.
Finish with tamarind pulp, green chilli and coriander leaf.
Boil the potatoes whole until a knife slides through, then peel.
Roast the dried chillies on a dry pan.
Mash the potato with salt, chilli and onion by hand.
Work in raw mustard oil and coriander leaf.
Rub the aubergine with a little oil and char it over an open flame until collapsed.
Cool, peel off the blackened skin and drain the liquid.
Mash with roasted garlic, chilli, onion and salt.
Fold in raw mustard oil and coriander leaf.
Roast the tomatoes over a flame until the skin blisters and peels.
Roast garlic and dried chilli on a dry pan.
Mash everything together with salt and onion.
Finish with mustard oil and coriander leaf.
Soak the dried fish in hot water 15 minutes, rinse twice and squeeze dry.
Roast it on a dry pan until crisp, then pound coarsely.
Fry onion, garlic and dried chilli in mustard oil until brown.
Pound everything together into a coarse paste and finish with coriander.
Toss the shrimp with turmeric and salt.
Fry in mustard oil until dry and slightly crisp; lift out.
In the same oil brown the onion, garlic and dried chilli.
Pound the shrimp with the fried aromatics and finish with coriander leaf.
Boil the fish with turmeric and salt, then flake and remove every bone.
Fry onion, garlic and chillies in mustard oil until soft and brown.
Add the flaked fish and fry until dry and fluffy.
Mash together and finish with coriander leaf.
Boil the lentil with very little water until thick and dry.
Roast garlic and dried chilli on a dry pan.
Mash the lentil with the roasted aromatics, onion and salt.
Work in raw mustard oil.
Dry-roast the nigella seeds until aromatic.
Roast garlic and dried chillies on the same pan.
Pound everything with salt to a coarse paste.
Mix in onion and raw mustard oil.
Soak the mustard seeds 30 minutes.
Grind with green chilli, garlic and salt to a smooth paste.
Rest 10 minutes to let the pungency develop.
Stir in mustard oil and coriander leaf.
Dry-roast the sesame until it begins to pop.
Roast garlic and chilli separately.
Grind together with salt to a coarse paste.
Mix in onion and a little mustard oil.
Roast the peanuts and rub off the skins.
Roast garlic and dried chilli.
Pound peanuts, garlic, chilli and salt to a coarse crumb.
Mix with onion, mustard oil and coriander leaf.
Steam or boil the pumpkin until soft and drain well.
Roast garlic and dried chilli.
Mash the pumpkin with salt, chilli, garlic and onion.
Finish with mustard oil and coriander leaf.
Boil the diced ash gourd until translucent.
Drain and squeeze out as much water as possible.
Mash with roasted garlic, chilli, onion and salt.
Stir in mustard oil and coriander leaf.
Steam the whole okra 8 minutes until just tender.
Roast garlic and dried chilli on a dry pan.
Chop and mash the okra with the roasted aromatics, onion and salt.
Finish with mustard oil and coriander leaf.
Boil the taro corms until completely soft, then peel.
Roast garlic and dried chilli.
Mash while warm with salt, onion and the roasted aromatics.
Work in raw mustard oil and coriander leaf.
Roast the dried chillies on a dry pan.
Pound them with salt.
Add sliced onion and crush by hand until juicy.
Mix in mustard oil and coriander leaf.
Temper nigella seeds in hot oil.
Add onion and green chilli, fry until translucent.
Add potato, turmeric and salt; toss to coat.
Sprinkle a little water, cover and cook 12 minutes until tender.
Finish uncovered with coriander leaf.
Lightly fry the cauliflower florets and set aside.
Temper bay leaf and cumin, then fry onion, ginger and garlic.
Add powdered spices and tomato, cook until the oil separates.
Add potato and water, cook 10 minutes, then return the cauliflower.
Simmer until both are tender and finish with coriander leaf.
Temper bay leaf and cumin in oil.
Fry onion and ginger, add potato and cook 5 minutes.
Add cabbage, peas, turmeric and salt.
Cover and cook on low 12 minutes, stirring so nothing catches.
Uncover and dry off any liquid before serving.
Slice the aubergine into thick rounds.
Rub with turmeric, chilli powder and salt; rest 10 minutes.
Shallow-fry in mustard oil over medium heat until brown on both sides.
Drain on paper before serving.
Peel, deseed and grate or julienne the green papaya.
Temper nigella and garlic in mustard oil.
Add onion and green chilli, fry 2 minutes.
Add papaya, turmeric and salt; cover and cook 12 minutes.
Uncover and stir until dry.
Scrape the gourd skin lightly and halve lengthwise.
Temper nigella in mustard oil, add onion.
Add potato and gourd with turmeric and salt.
Cover and cook 12-14 minutes, turning once.
Finish with green chilli.
Peel the ridges off the gourd and dice.
Temper nigella, garlic and onion in mustard oil.
Add potato and cook 5 minutes.
Add gourd, turmeric and salt; cover and cook 10 minutes.
Uncover and reduce until nearly dry.
Wash and dry the okra thoroughly before cutting.
Fry garlic and onion in mustard oil.
Add okra, turmeric, chilli powder and salt.
Stir-fry uncovered 12-14 minutes until the edges brown.
Add green chilli in the last minute.
String the beans and slice them on the diagonal.
Temper nigella and garlic in mustard oil.
Add onion, then potato and beans with turmeric and salt.
Cover and cook 15 minutes, sprinkling water if needed.
Finish with green chillies.
Cut the beans into short lengths.
Fry garlic and onion in mustard oil until soft.
Add beans, turmeric, chilli powder and salt.
Cover and cook 12 minutes until tender-crisp.
Uncover, dry off and add green chilli.
Temper nigella and fenugreek in mustard oil.
Add garlic and onion, fry until soft.
Add pumpkin, turmeric and salt.
Cover and cook 15 minutes until it collapses slightly.
Mash a little against the pan and finish with green chilli.
Clean the shrimp and toss with turmeric and salt.
Fry the shrimp briefly in mustard oil and lift out.
Fry onion, garlic and ginger, add cumin and turmeric.
Add the diced gourd, cover and let it cook in its own water 12 minutes.
Return the shrimp, add green chillies and simmer 5 minutes.
Peel and halve the taro corms, then par-boil with salt.
Fry the shrimp in mustard oil and lift out.
Fry onion, garlic and ginger, add the powdered spices with a splash of water.
Add the taro and water, simmer 15 minutes until soft.
Return the shrimp, add green chillies and reduce to a thick gravy.
Temper nigella in mustard oil, then fry garlic and onion.
Add radish and potato with turmeric and salt.
Cover and cook 15 minutes in the radish's own water.
Uncover, raise the heat and stir until dry.
Finish with green chillies.
Slice the bitter gourd thin and rub with a little salt; rest 10 minutes.
Squeeze out the bitter juice and pat dry.
Fry garlic and onion in mustard oil.
Add potato, gourd, turmeric and chilli powder.
Stir-fry uncovered 12 minutes until the edges are crisp.
Cut all vegetables to a similar size so they cook evenly.
Temper bay leaf and cumin, fry onion, ginger and garlic.
Add turmeric and coriander powder with a splash of water.
Add the hard vegetables first, then the softer ones after 8 minutes.
Add water and salt, cover and simmer until tender; finish with coriander.
Mix cumin, fennel, fenugreek, nigella and mustard seed to make panch phoron.
Temper it with bay leaf and dried chilli in hot mustard oil.
Add ginger, turmeric and all the vegetables.
Cover and cook on low, letting the vegetables release their own water.
Stir occasionally for 25 minutes until soft and merged.
Fry the bitter gourd slices separately and set aside.
Temper fenugreek in mustard oil, add ginger.
Add the remaining vegetables and cook briefly.
Add water, mustard and poppy paste; simmer until tender.
Stir in milk, return the bitter gourd, finish with ghee.
Fry the scraped gourd and potato pieces until golden; set aside.
Temper bay leaf and cumin in the same oil.
Add ginger, tomato and powdered spices; cook until oil separates.
Return the vegetables, add water and salt.
Simmer covered 15 minutes until the gravy thickens.
Scrape the tough skin off the drumsticks and cut into finger lengths.
Fry onion and garlic in mustard oil.
Add turmeric, cumin and mustard paste with a splash of water.
Add the vegetables and water, cover and cook 15 minutes.
Finish with green chillies and a drizzle of raw mustard oil.
Wash the spinach in several changes of water and chop.
Temper nigella and dried chilli in hot mustard oil.
Add garlic and onion and fry until golden.
Add the spinach and salt, stir-fry uncovered 6-8 minutes until the water dries.
Pick, wash and chop the amaranth leaves and tender stems.
Fry garlic and dried chilli in mustard oil until fragrant.
Add onion, then the greens and salt.
Stir-fry uncovered until the released water evaporates, about 8 minutes.
Separate the stems from the leaves and chop both.
Fry the turmeric-rubbed shrimp in mustard oil and lift out.
Fry garlic and onion, add potato and the stems.
After 6 minutes add the leaves and salt.
Return the shrimp, add green chilli and cook until dry.
Wash the greens in at least three changes of water.
Temper nigella and dried chilli in mustard oil.
Add garlic and onion and fry until golden.
Add the chopped greens and salt; stir-fry 8 minutes until dry.
Strip the leaves from the stalks and wash well.
Temper nigella, garlic and dried chilli in mustard oil.
Add onion, then the leaves and salt.
Stir-fry 10 minutes until soft; squeeze lemon over before serving.
Peel the fibrous skin off the tender vines and chop with the leaves.
Temper nigella and dried chilli in mustard oil.
Fry garlic and onion, add turmeric.
Add the greens and salt, cover 5 minutes, then dry off uncovered.
Chop the radish leaves finely and wash.
Temper nigella and dried chilli in mustard oil.
Fry garlic, onion and diced potato until half done.
Add the greens and salt, cook uncovered 10 minutes until dry.
Strip the leaves from the stalks; this is the slow part.
Wash and drain thoroughly.
Fry garlic, onion and dried chilli in mustard oil.
Add the leaves, turmeric and salt; stir-fry 6-8 minutes only.
Rub the steaks with turmeric, chilli powder and salt; rest 15 minutes.
Heat mustard oil until it just smokes, then lower the heat.
Fry the pieces 4-5 minutes per side until crisp at the edges.
Drain and serve with plain rice.
Soak mustard seed with a little salt and green chilli, then grind to a smooth paste.
Rub the fish with turmeric and salt.
Warm mustard oil, temper nigella, then add the mustard paste with water.
Slide in the fish and simmer 10-12 minutes without stirring.
Add whole green chillies and raw mustard oil at the end.
Grind mustard seed, coconut and green chilli to a paste.
Mix with yoghurt, turmeric, salt and mustard oil.
Coat the fish steaks and place them in a sealed tiffin box.
Set the box in a pan of simmering water and steam 20-25 minutes.
Rub the fish with turmeric and salt and fry lightly; set aside.
In the same oil fry onion, ginger and garlic.
Add tomato and powdered spices, cook until the oil separates.
Add potato and water, simmer 10 minutes.
Return the fish, simmer 8 minutes, finish with chilli and coriander.
Fry the turmeric-and-salt rubbed fish until golden; set aside.
Fry the potatoes in the same oil.
Temper whole spices, add onion paste and cook until deep brown.
Add ginger, garlic, yoghurt and powdered spices; cook until oil separates.
Return fish and potato with a little water, simmer 12 minutes, finish with ghee.
Fry the seasoned fish lightly and lift out.
Fry cauliflower and potato in the same oil until spotted brown.
Fry onion and ginger, add tomato and spices.
Add water and vegetables, simmer 12 minutes.
Return the fish and cook 8 minutes more; finish with coriander.
Fry the turmeric-rubbed fish lightly and set aside.
Temper whole spices, fry onion paste and ginger until pale gold.
Take the pan off the heat and whisk in the yoghurt.
Return to low heat, add the fish and a little water.
Simmer gently 12 minutes, finish with ghee and green chilli.
Devein the prawns, keeping the heads on, and rub with turmeric and salt.
Sear them briefly in mustard oil and lift out.
Temper whole spices, fry onion paste and ginger until golden.
Add powdered spices, then the coconut milk and sugar.
Return the prawns, simmer 8 minutes only, finish with ghee and chillies.
Clean and devein the prawns, toss with turmeric and salt.
Sear in hot mustard oil for 2 minutes and lift out.
Brown the onion, garlic and ginger.
Add tomato and powdered spices, cook until the oil separates.
Return the prawns, cook 6 minutes until dry, finish with coriander.
Clean the fish whole and rub with turmeric and salt.
Fry very briefly in mustard oil and lift out carefully.
Temper nigella, add onion, ginger, cumin and mustard paste.
Add water and bring to a simmer, then slide the fish in.
Cook 8 minutes without stirring; finish with chilli and coriander.
Clean the small fish and rub with turmeric and salt.
Temper nigella in mustard oil, fry onion and ginger.
Add powdered spices, potato and aubergine, then water.
When the vegetables are half cooked, slide in the fish.

Fry in hot mustard oil until firm, then set aside.
Temper nigella, add onion and the mustard paste with water.
Simmer the gravy 5 minutes, then return the fish.
Cook 10 minutes and finish with whole green chillies.
Clean the fish thoroughly and rub with turmeric and salt.
Fry lightly in mustard oil and lift out.
Fry onion, garlic and ginger, add cumin and turmeric.
Add the chopped amaranth and cook until wilted.
Add water and the fish, simmer 10 minutes with green chillies.
Clean the fish well with salt and rub with turmeric.

Fry onion, ginger and garlic, add cumin and turmeric.
Add potato and water, cook 10 minutes.
Return the fish, simmer 8 minutes, finish with chilli and coriander.
Rub the fish with turmeric and salt, fry lightly and set aside.
Fry onion, garlic and ginger until brown.
Add powdered spices with a splash of water and cook until oil separates.
Add potato and water, simmer 12 minutes.
Return the fish and cook 8 minutes more.
Rub the steaks with turmeric and salt and fry until golden.

Add tomato and all powdered spices, cook until the oil separates.
Return the fish with a little water.
Cook uncovered 12 minutes until the masala is thick and dry.
Scrape the flesh off the bones and mix with mashed potato, half the onion and spices.

Fry the remaining onion, garlic and ginger with whole spices.
Add powdered spices and water to make a gravy.
Slip the koftas in and simmer 12 minutes; finish with coriander.

Fry onion, garlic and ginger, add tomato and powdered spices.
Add potato and water, simmer 10 minutes.
Return the fish, cook 8 minutes and finish with green chilli.

Marinate with turmeric, chilli, garlic, lemon juice and salt for 20 minutes.
Shallow-fry in hot mustard oil 6 minutes per side.
Drain and serve with rice and dal.
Slash the fish diagonally on both sides.
Rub in garlic, ginger, turmeric, chilli, pepper, lemon and salt; rest 30 minutes.
Shallow-fry on medium heat 7 minutes per side.
Rest 2 minutes before serving so the flesh sets.

Roast it briefly and cut into pieces.
Brown onion, garlic and ginger in mustard oil.
Add tomato and powdered spices, cook until oil separates.
Add the fish and a little water, cook 15 minutes until dry.

Fry onion, garlic and potato in mustard oil.
Add turmeric, chilli powder and salt.

Rest briefly and serve with coriander and lemon.
Marinate the beef with ginger, garlic, powdered spices and salt for 30 minutes.
Brown the onions in mustard oil with the whole spices.
Add the meat and fry on high heat until it changes colour.

Add the fried onion to the meat and continue cooking uncovered.
Keep stirring 25-30 minutes until the meat is very dark and dry.
Brown the onion in oil with the whole spices.
Add ginger, garlic and powdered spices with a splash of water.
Add the beef and fry until sealed, then add hot water.
Cover and cook 55 minutes until nearly tender.
Add the potatoes and cook 20 minutes more until both are soft.

Add the marinated meat and cook covered on low heat until tender.

Add powdered spices and tomato, cook until the oil separates.
Add the mince and break up the lumps as it browns.
Add peas and a little water, cook 20 minutes until dry.
Finish with pepper and coriander leaf.

Simmer 10 minutes and finish with coriander leaf.

Fry the potato wedges in the same oil.

Fold in raw mustard oil and coriander leaf.
